# Lab 4.3: Working with Arrays & Structs

## What We Are Going to Do
Build, read and flatten arrays and structs with ARRAY_AGG, ARRAY_CONCAT, GENERATE_ARRAY, OFFSET and STRUCT.

## Steps

1. **[SQL] Build arrays.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT
  GENERATE_ARRAY(1, 10, 3) AS steps,
  ARRAY_CONCAT([1, 2], [3, 4]) AS joined,
  ARRAY_LENGTH(['a', 'b', 'c']) AS len,
  ['red', 'green', 'blue'][OFFSET(0)] AS first_zero_based,
  ['red', 'green', 'blue'][ORDINAL(1)] AS first_one_based,
  ['red', 'green', 'blue'][SAFE_OFFSET(10)] AS safe_out_of_range;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[SQL] Aggregate rows into arrays of structs.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">CREATE TABLE lab04.user_orders AS
SELECT
  user_id,
  ARRAY_AGG(STRUCT(order_id, status, created_at) ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 5) AS last_orders
FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.orders`
GROUP BY user_id;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


3. **[SQL] Read struct fields and filter inside arrays.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT
  user_id,
  last_orders[SAFE_OFFSET(0)].status AS latest_status,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM UNNEST(last_orders) o WHERE o.status = 'Returned') AS returns
FROM lab04.user_orders
LIMIT 10;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


4. **[SQL] Flatten, keeping empty arrays.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">WITH t AS (SELECT 1 AS id, [10, 20] AS vals UNION ALL SELECT 2, [])
SELECT id, v FROM t LEFT JOIN UNNEST(vals) AS v;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Row `2` stays with `v = NULL`. With a comma (cross) join it would disappear.

5. **[Console] Preview the nested table.** Open `lab04.user_orders → Preview` and expand `last_orders` for one user.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| `OFFSET` | Zero-based; `ORDINAL` is one-based |
| `SAFE_OFFSET` | Returns NULL instead of an error |
| `ARRAY_AGG(STRUCT …)` | Last 5 orders per user in one row |
| `LEFT JOIN UNNEST` | Keeps rows with empty arrays |
